points.title: Flowchart, algorithm, process design
points.must: Flowchart = diagram of the steps of one process in order with standard symbols and flow lines; algorithm = finite sequence of clear steps; process design = planning the logic of every DFD process before coding.

points.title: Process design in the life cycle and IPO
points.must: Design stage after analysis; process design answers: inputs, processing, decisions/repetitions, outputs (input → process → output).

points.title: The flowchart symbols
points.must: Terminator (START/END), process rectangle (assignment/calculation), parallelogram (INPUT/OUTPUT), diamond (Yes/No question, two labelled exits), subroutine (double sides), flow line — each drawn with an example.

points.title: DFD vs flowchart
points.must: DFD = what processes exist and how data flows (whole system, no decisions); flowchart = how one process works; DFD flows in/out become the flowchart's inputs/outputs, data stores become read/save steps.

points.title: Why design before coding; advantages and disadvantages
points.must: Errors cheaper to fix on paper, client can check the logic, each decision gives test paths, part of documentation; disadvantages: large diagrams, slow to change.

points.title: Rules for a good flowchart
points.must: One START and an END, top to bottom with arrowheads, two labelled exits per decision, one step per box, correct symbols.

points.title: Sequence
points.must: Steps run once in order; order matters (output after the calculation; swapping two variables needs temp).

points.title: Selection patterns
points.must: IF…THEN…ELSE, IF…THEN without ELSE, nested IF for more than two outcomes; branches join again (ENDIF); a drawn example with Yes/No exits.

points.title: Worked example with boundary testing
points.must: Cinema price (under 12 → 1500 ₸, otherwise 2500 ₸) tested with values below, on and above the boundary (11, 12).

points.title: Nested selection
points.must: Grade from a mark with decisions 85 / 70 / 50 checked from the highest boundary down.

points.title: Conditions and operators
points.must: =, <>, <, <=, >, >=, AND, OR, NOT with examples; range 11–18 written with AND; one AND diamond = two nested diamonds.

points.title: Processes in computing systems
points.must: Common pattern: input → checks (one diamond each, error message on No) → calculate → save to data store → output; definitions of process, subroutine, data store.

points.title: Worked example: issuing a library book or vending machine
points.must: A full flowchart for one real process: inputs, checks in a sensible order, calculation, data store, output, and a test for every exit (e.g. 4 and 5 books, 299 and 300 ₸).

points.title: Subroutines and top-down design
points.must: A big process split into subroutines drawn once and called many times; easier to read, change and share between programmers.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: Wrong shapes, decision with one exit / unlabelled, wrong boundary (< vs <=), OR instead of AND, error path continuing into the main work, missing save step.
